name: collapsing-columns
title: Collapsing columns
description: Equal columns that stack all at once when their own container gets narrow, with no awkward two-plus-one in between.
docs: The cells are the children, two to five of them. threshold is the width of the container, any CSS length, below which they stack in one step (40rem by default). It is measured on the content width of this element, never on the window, so the same component is a row on a wide page and a column in a sidebar or a dialog, with no media query and no script. gap is none, sm, md, lg or a length, and applies between the columns and between the rows once stacked; align is start, center, end or stretch (the default: equal heights); as is div, section, ul or ol, with li cells for a list. The cells share the width evenly and may shrink to nothing, so a long word breaks instead of widening its cell. The source order is the stacked order.
